title: Earthquakes, live
blurb: Every earthquake recorded in the past hour, day, week or month, updated every minute. Colour by mag and you'll see how many small quakes happen that never make the news.

title: Fires burning right now
blurb: Every fire hotspot satellites detected in the last 24 hours, 48 hours or 7 days. Colour by frp (fire power) to find the fiercest, or filter daynight to compare day and night.

title: Every US tornado since 1950
blurb: 73,458 tornado paths from 1950 to 2025, each with its strength, injuries, deaths, length and width. Colour by mag and Tornado Alley draws itself. Hail and wind reports are on the same page.

title: Sea surface temperature since 1854
blurb: Monthly ocean surface temperatures back to January 1854, rebuilt from ship, buoy and Argo float measurements. Step through the years and look for El Niño warming the eastern Pacific.
source: NOAA ERSST v5, via NOAA PSL

title: Rain and snow everywhere since 1979
blurb: Monthly precipitation in mm per day for the whole globe since January 1979, from satellites and rain gauges. Step through one year and watch the monsoon rains move over Asia.

title: Every wind turbine in the United States
blurb: 77,839 turbines, each with the year it was built (1982 to 2026), its height and its capacity. Colour by year (p_year) and watch wind power spread across the Great Plains.
source: US Wind Turbine Database v9.1 (USGS, LBNL, ACP)

title: Nuclear power reactors of the world
blurb: 804 reactors, operating, under construction, planned or shut down, with reactor type and capacity. Filter by Status to see where new ones are being built.

title: Solar farms seen from space
blurb: 68,661 solar power installations, outlined by machine learning on satellite images as they stood at the end of 2018. Open trn_polygons.geojson and zoom in to see the real shapes of the panel fields.

title: The world's mines, outlined
blurb: 44,929 mining areas covering 101,583 km², including open pits, tailings dams and waste dumps, traced by hand from satellite images. Colour by AREA to find the giants. Download the single .gpkg file; the all-files zip asks for an account.

title: World cities with population
blurb: A fuller list than the cities NimbleMap bundles: about 50,000 cities and towns with population and country codes. Colour by population, or filter capital to show only capitals.

title: Life expectancy, every country
blurb: This table has no coordinates, only a Code column of country codes, so join it to NimbleMap's countries and filter by Year. Global life expectancy went from 32 years in 1900 to 73 in 2023.

title: Where people live, 1 km grid
blurb: Estimated number of people in every 1 km cell, for any country and any year from 2000 to 2020. Pick China and click cells either side of the Hu Line to compare.

title: Every airport, airstrip and heliport
blurb: The full version of the bundled airports layer, updated daily: 42,820 small airstrips, 23,248 heliports, 1,273 seaplane bases, even 63 balloonports. Filter type to find the 13,574 closed ones.

title: World Port Index
blurb: 3,807 seaports, each with more than 100 details such as harbour size, channel depth and the longest ship it can take. Colour by Channel Depth (m) to see which ports take the biggest ships.

title: Japan's railways and stations
blurb: Every passenger railway and tram line in Japan, with operator and line name, plus every station. Open the GeoJSON files in the UTF-8 folder and colour lines by operator (N02_004). Names are in Japanese.
source: National Land Numerical Information N02, MLIT Japan

title: UNESCO World Heritage sites
blurb: Every World Heritage site, with its category (991 cultural, 240 natural, 42 mixed), the year it was inscribed and whether it is in danger. Colour by category, or filter by year.

title: Pleiades: places of the ancient world
blurb: A gazetteer of 42,404 ancient places, updated several times a week. Download the GIS zip, open places.csv, and use representative_latitude and representative_longitude as coordinates.

title: Roads of the Roman Empire
blurb: The roads of the Roman Empire from about 300 BCE to 300 CE, 299,171 km of them, almost double earlier maps. Lay them over today's motorways and see how many still follow the same line.

title: China's county seats, 221 BCE to 1911
blurb: Every county seat of imperial China with the year it was set up (BEG_YR) and abolished (END_YR), named in Chinese and pinyin. Filter by year and watch dynasties redraw the map.
source: CHGIS V6, Harvard University and Fudan University

title: Buddhist temples of China
blurb: 18,938 Buddhist temples and sites from a 2006 national directory, with Chinese and pinyin names, type and province. Colour by province (PROV_HZ) to see where temples cluster.
source: BGIS (University of Arizona), via Harvard Dataverse

title: Castles, from Wikidata
blurb: Press Run (it takes about 30 seconds), then Download › CSV file. You get about 23,000 castles with a geometry column that NimbleMap reads as points. Change Q23413 in the query to map lighthouses, monasteries or anything else.

title: White stork migrations, 1991–2017
blurb: Satellite tracks of more than 200 white storks tagged in nine countries. One of them, Prinzesschen, was followed for over a decade. Filter by bird (individual-local-identifier) and trace the flyways between Europe and Africa.
source: Max Planck Institute, Movebank Data Repository

title: New York City's street trees
blurb: 683,788 street trees, each with species, trunk diameter and health. Colour by health, or filter spc_common to find every ginkgo in the city.
source: NYC Parks 2015 Street Tree Census, NYC Open Data
licence: NYC Open Data, free to use

title: Global forest loss, 2001–2025
blurb: A 30-metre map of where forest was cleared, each pixel coded with the year it was lost (2001 to 2025). Download the lossyear tile for your region and click a pixel to read the year.

title: Every known meteorite
blurb: 45,716 meteorites with mass, class, year and whether someone saw it fall. Use reclat and reclong as coordinates, colour by mass (g) and find the giants.

title: Paths of the 2023 and 2024 solar eclipses
blurb: The exact path of totality of the 8 April 2024 eclipse, with duration contours every 30 seconds and bands showing how much of the Sun was covered. The October 2023 annular eclipse is there too.

title: Earth at night
blurb: The planet's city lights in 2012 and 2016, as GeoTIFFs at 0.1°, 3 km or 500 m. Put the bundled cities on top and see which glow brightest.

title: Chain stores, brand by brand
blurb: Store and branch locations collected every week from brand websites: Starbucks, McDonald's, IKEA and thousands more. Search a brand, click Feature GeoJSON, and compare chains city by city.

title: Anything on OpenStreetMap: overpass turbo
blurb: Open the Wizard, type something like shop=mall in Shanghai or amenity=drinking_water in Paris, press Run, then Export › GeoJSON.

title: Your city from OpenStreetMap: BBBike extracts
blurb: Draw a box around any city, choose Shapefile or GeoJSON, and you get an email when your extract of roads, buildings and shops is ready to download.

title: A whole country from OpenStreetMap: Geofabrik
blurb: Ready-made OpenStreetMap downloads for every country and many regions. The free .shp.zip splits roads, railways, buildings, places of worship and points of interest into separate layers.

title: Singapore's hawker centres
blurb: All 129 hawker centres in Singapore, existing and under construction, with addresses and photo links. Colour by STATUS for a small, tasty first map.
